text: The court held that the agency had gone too far on that record.
The judge noted that the notice was late, without deciding anything about it.
She told me the appeal would be filed the following week.
He asked what I thought of the dissent.
Two judges dissented, and the dissent is the part everybody is quoting.
That is what it decided; it is not what it decided about everybody else.

The first thing I do is not read the judgment. I read the last three pages, because that is where the court tells you what it actually decided, and everything before it is the argument for it. Then I go looking for one sentence: the one that would change if the case had come out the other way. That sentence is the decision. Everything else, however quotable, is either background or somebody being interesting. The mistake I made for years was quoting the best line I found, and the best line is very often in the dissent, because dissents are written to be read and majority opinions are written to be survived. Now I write the label first. The court held. Two judges disagreed. This does not decide the wider question. If those three sentences are true, I can make the rest as readable as I like.

I give every junior who joins us one rule about reporting a decision, and it is not about research. Never report with a stronger verb than the court used. If the judgment says the court noted something, you write noted. If it observed, you write observed. The temptation is enormous, because a memo that says the court held is more useful to the person reading it than a memo that says the court noted, and for about a week nobody finds out. Then somebody relies on your sentence in front of a client, or worse, in front of another court, and the whole thing comes back to the paragraph where you upgraded a verb. I have seen it happen twice. Both times the person was excellent and simply wanted to be helpful. Being helpful is what the rule is there to protect you from.

The judgment is handed down and runs to ninety pages. The last pages are read first, because that is where the court says what it decided. One sentence is identified: the one that would change if the case had gone the other way. The dissent is labelled as a dissent, so that nobody quotes it as the decision. And the summary is written with the verb the court used, and never a stronger one.
